feat(mcp): add AuthorizationServerMismatchError for OAuth pin mismatches (#20560)

## Background

`assertAuthorizationServerInformationMatches` throws a bare
`MCPClientOAuthError` when stored credentials were issued by a different
authorization server. Consumers need to treat this case as permanent
(drop credentials, reconnect) rather than retry, but the only handle
today is matching the message string — every other case in
`oauth-error.ts` has a subclass with a `static errorCode`.

## Summary

- Add `AuthorizationServerMismatchError` (`errorCode:
'authorization_server_mismatch'`), following the existing subclass
pattern, and throw it at the mismatch site. Message unchanged. Not added
to `OAUTH_ERRORS`, which maps server-reported wire codes; this is a
client-side check.
- Export it and `MCPClientOAuthError` from the entrypoint so
`isInstance` is reachable (neither was exported).
- The existing end-to-end mismatch test in `oauth.test.ts` now asserts
the subclass, not just the message. Patch changeset added.

## Verification

`pnpm --filter @ai-sdk/mcp test`: 319 passed, 3 skipped (unchanged) on
both node and edge configs. `type-check` clean.

## Checklist

- [x] All commits are signed (PRs with unsigned commits cannot be
merged)

- [ ] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)

docs(black-forest-labs): document FLUX.2 image models (#20060)

## Summary

Stacked on #20020, which this branch is built on. The FLUX 3 video
commit from that PR is included here; only the second commit is new.

The Black Forest Labs provider page and the AI SDK Core image model
table list only FLUX.1 models (`flux-kontext-*`, `flux-pro-1.*`). The
five FLUX.2 image models are callable through
`@ai-sdk/black-forest-labs` today and through AI Gateway as
`bfl/flux-2-*`, but they are undocumented, so there is no way to
discover them from the docs.

This PR:

- Adds `flux-2-pro`, `flux-2-max`, `flux-2-flex`, `flux-2-klein-9b`, and
`flux-2-klein-4b` to the provider page model table and to the image
model table in `ai-sdk-core/image-generation`.
- Documents that FLUX.2 accepts reference images on the same
`prompt.images` field as Kontext, so one model ID covers both
text-to-image and editing.
- Documents `steps` and `guidance` on `flux-2-flex`.
- Notes that FLUX.2 generations can exceed the 60s default polling
timeout and that `pollTimeoutMillis` should be raised.
- Adds an Image Models section to the AI Gateway provider page, which
previously documented video generation but not image generation.

Documentation only. No SDK, provider, or test changes.

## Verification

Every model ID and behavior was confirmed against the live API using the
existing provider code, not inferred from docs:

- `bfl/flux-2-pro`, `bfl/flux-2-max`, `bfl/flux-2-flex`,
`bfl/flux-2-klein-9b`, `bfl/flux-2-klein-4b` all appear in `GET
https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models` with `type: image`.
- `generateImage` with `blackForestLabs.image(flux-2-pro | flux-2-flex |
flux-2-klein-9b | flux-2-klein-4b)` returned image bytes with no
warnings.
- Reference-image editing verified on `flux-2-pro` (one and two
references) and `flux-2-klein-9b` via `prompt.images`.
- `steps: 50, guidance: 4` accepted on `flux-2-flex`; `aspectRatio:
21:9` accepted on `flux-2-pro`.
- The polling note comes from observed `Black Forest Labs generation
timed out.` failures at the 60s default that succeeded at 240000ms.

Local checks: `oxfmt --check` on all three files, `pnpm validate:docs`,
`pnpm --filter ai-sdk-docs test:site` (9/9), `pnpm --filter ai-sdk-docs
type-check:site`, `git diff --check`. All passed.

---------

Co-authored-by: Aayush Kapoor <aayushkapoor34@gmail.com>

fix: propagate createUIMessageStream consumer cancellation to merged streams (#21728)

## Background

Consumer cancellation of createUIMessageStream did not stop merged
sources, allowing upstream requests and pending pulls to continue after
disconnection.

## Root Cause

writer.merge() consumed each source through an untracked reader, so the
returned stream's cancellation path had no reader to cancel. The
original reproduction confirmed that the source cancel handler was not
invoked and its pending pull continued.

## Summary

Track active merged-stream readers, cancel them with the consumer's
reason, immediately cancel streams merged after cancellation, and
release reader locks after completion.

## Testing

Added a regression test confirming that consumer cancellation reaches
the merged source and prevents its pending pull from producing another
chunk.

## End-to-end Validation

- `replay_original_reproduction` restored and ran `pnpm -C
examples/ai-functions exec tsx
src/reproduction/issue-21721-merged-stream-cancellation.ts`; it exited
successfully and reported that issue #21721 no longer reproduced.

## Related Issues

Fixes #21721

Closes #21725

---------

fix: prevent streamed useChat updates from starving App Router navigation (#21874)

## Background

While `useChat` streamed a response, synchronous external-store
notifications could repeatedly interrupt Next.js App Router navigation
and delay it by about five seconds.

## Summary

- Store messages, status, and error together in one React state snapshot
and publish ordinary React state updates. This prevents navigation
starvation while allowing streamed text and local edits to render during
suspended transitions.
- Reset the snapshot during render when the Chat instance changes, use
pure snapshot updaters, and resynchronize after subscribing to catch
changes between render and subscription.
- Preserve throttling, shared-chat subscriptions, cleanup, and
consistent completion/error/abort snapshots without adding configuration
or a separate terminal-message cache.
- Restore coverage for streaming during suspended id changes and add
regression tests for streamed text and local edits during suspended
sibling navigation.

## Validation

- The three suspended-transition regression checks failed before the
local follow-up changes and passed afterward.
- React 18.3.1: all 145 React package tests passed.
- React 19.2.6: all 54 `useChat` tests passed.
- Package build, full workspace type-check, lint, formatting, and diff
checks passed.
- Production Next.js 16.3.3 with an unthrottled deterministic stream and
4× CPU throttling: updated `useChat` navigated in 867 ms versus 5,587 ms
for an external-store control (single runs).
- In a three-second sample with an expensive synthetic chat render under
4× CPU throttling, the updated hook had a maximum visible-update gap of
33 ms.

The latest follow-up implementation changes and validation are local;
they have not been committed or pushed.

Fixes #21849
Closes #21854

---------

docs(site): add Black Forest Labs to the model picker (#20063)

## Summary

The interactive code preview on the docs site allowlists providers per
model kind. Black Forest Labs is absent from both the image and video
allowlists, so FLUX models never appear in the picker on
`ai-sdk-core/image-generation` and `ai-sdk-core/video-generation`, even
though the models are served by the gateway endpoint the picker itself
reads from. Black Forest Labs also has no entry in `PROVIDER_LOGOS`, so
its models would render with the generic placeholder mark.

This PR:

- Adds `bfl` to the `image` and `video` provider allowlists.
- Sets `bfl/flux-2-pro` and `bfl/flux-3-video` as the preferred defaults
when a reader selects Black Forest Labs.
- Adds a `providerSdkMap` entry so the Provider tab generates `import {
blackForestLabs } from "@ai-sdk/black-forest-labs"` rather than the
incorrect `@ai-sdk/bfl` / `bfl` that the fallback would produce.
- Adds the provider's logo so its models render with the real mark
instead of the generic fallback.

No behavior changes for any other provider.

## The logo asset

`apps/docs/public/images/icons/black-forest-labs.svg` is the official
symbol-only mark from [bfl.ai/brand](https://bfl.ai/brand), which the
brand guidelines designate for small applications where the wordmark
would be unreadable.

- Path data and `viewBox` are byte-identical to the published
`symbol-black.svg`.
- The only changes: `fill` is `currentColor` instead of the fixed
`#07130e`, and a `clipPath` wrapper was dropped. That clip was a
full-canvas `M0 0h196v140H0z` rect, so removing it is a no-op. Using
`currentColor` lets the existing `invert: true` dark-mode handling work,
the same treatment already applied to the Anthropic and xAI marks.

## Verification

- `GET https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models` returns
`bfl/flux-3-video` with `type: video`, and `bfl/flux-2-pro`,
`bfl/flux-2-max`, `bfl/flux-2-flex`, `bfl/flux-2-klein-9b`,
`bfl/flux-2-klein-4b` with `type: image`.
- `parseModels` keys on `owned_by`, not the model ID prefix, so I
confirmed `owned_by` is exactly `bfl` for all 11 models rather than
assuming it from the ID. Replaying the real filter against the live
response with this patch applied yields 10 FLUX models in the image
picker and `bfl/flux-3-video` in the video picker; without it, zero.
- `providerTitles` already contains `bfl: 'Black Forest Labs'`, so the
label renders correctly with no further change.
- The package name and export were confirmed against
`packages/black-forest-labs` (`@ai-sdk/black-forest-labs`, exports
`blackForestLabs`), so the Provider tab snippet is copy-pasteable.
- Verified the committed SVG renders as the complete BFL peak mark, not
a clipped or corrupted path.
- `oxfmt --check` on the changed file passes.

Note on scope: `FIRST_PARTY_PROVIDERS` is deliberately untouched. It
feeds the text-model preview, and this provider exposes no language
model (`languageModel` throws `NoSuchModelError`), so it does not belong
in that list.

I was not able to visually confirm the rendered dropdown: the local docs
dev server ran out of memory on this machine before serving a page.
Flagging that rather than claiming a visual check I did not complete.
The logic change is data-only and confined to three lookup tables, and
the Docs Site CI job covers the build.

The same logo asset is added by #20079, which adds the provider index
card. Whichever merges first, the other's copy is identical (sha256
`cf8b6a00ff0752743ea35ec4b61485befc355d7d2469b6f417ea9c30037ed899`), so
the overlap resolves cleanly.

---------

Co-authored-by: Aayush Kapoor <aayushkapoor34@gmail.com>

feat(azure): support MAI-Voice-2.1 speech and MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming (#21910)

## Background

Microsoft AI launched MAI-Voice-2.1, MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash, and
MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming on Azure. #21851 and #21850 added MAI-Voice-2
and MAI-Transcribe-1.5 to `@ai-sdk/azure`. This PR adds the new models
on top of that work.

- **MAI-Voice-2.1 and MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash** use the same Azure Speech
(SSML) path as MAI-Voice-2. They only need their Azure model names.
- **MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming** is a different API: the MAI realtime
WebSocket
(`wss://{resourceName}.services.ai.azure.com/mai/v1/realtime?intent=transcription`).
It's OpenAI-realtime-compatible, but it doesn't detect pauses on the
server. Its `transcription.model` is the Foundry deployment name, not
the model name.

## Summary

**Speech**
- `mai-voice-2.1` and `mai-voice-2.1-flash` (case-insensitive) use Azure
Speech by default and send `MAI-Voice-2.1` / `MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash` as
the SSML voice-name suffix. The existing per-language default voices are
available on both models.
- Azure Speech resets the connection for an unknown voice or style (an
Envoy 502 with `reset reason: protocol error`). That case now fails with
a descriptive, non-retryable error. All other 502s stay retryable, as
before.

**Streaming transcription**
- `azure.transcription('mai-transcribe-2-streaming')` streams to the MAI
realtime API with `experimental_streamTranscribe`. The model ID is sent
as the deployment name. For a deployment with a different name, set
`providerOptions.azure.api: 'mai'`.
- **Input:** 16-bit mono PCM (`audio/pcm`) at 16000 or 24000 Hz; the
default is 24000. Other formats and rates are rejected with
`InvalidArgumentError`.
- **Output:** `transcript-delta` parts carry finalized text and
`transcript-partial` parts carry the provisional text after the latest
delta. The stream commits once when the input audio ends, then emits
`transcript-final`. `durationInSeconds` is computed from the streamed
audio.
- **Options:** `providerOptions.azure.language` is a language hint.
File-transcription options such as `timestamps` produce warnings when
streaming.
- **Not supported:** `doGenerate` on this model throws
`UnsupportedFunctionalityError` (no file transcription), and `api:
'speech'` can't stream.

**Provider settings**
- `maiBaseURL` overrides the MAI realtime URL prefix (default
`https://{resourceName}.services.ai.azure.com/mai/v1`).
- `webSocket` takes a custom WebSocket implementation such as `ws`. With
one, the API key is sent in the `api-key` header; with the native
`WebSocket` it's sent as the `api-key` query parameter. Microsoft Entra
ID (`tokenProvider`) needs a custom implementation.

**Docs and examples**
- The Azure provider page gains the 2.1 models, a
MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming section, the new settings, and capability
rows. The core speech and transcription model tables are updated too.
- New examples:
`examples/ai-functions/src/generate-speech/azure/mai-voice-2-1.ts` and
`examples/ai-functions/src/stream-transcribe/azure/basic.ts`.

## End-to-End Verification

All runs used a Microsoft Foundry resource with the models available:

- **Voices:** `generate-speech/azure/mai-voice-2-1.ts` with both 2.1
models. Voices tested: `en-US-Harper`, `en-US-Grant`, `en-US-Sage`,
`de-DE-Harper`, `fr-FR-Harper`, `en-GB-Emily`. Styles tested:
`narrator`, `agent`, `educational`, `joyful`. All 15 per-language
default voices return audio on both models.
- **Unknown voice or style:** returns the new descriptive error once,
with no client retries.
- **Streaming:** `stream-transcribe/azure/basic.ts` streamed PCM
generated by MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash and returned the expected transcript at
24 kHz and 16 kHz, with `ws` and the native `WebSocket`.
`durationInSeconds` matched the audio length.
- **Through AI Gateway:** the same models run in production, using a
build of this branch.

## Checklist

- [x] All commits are signed (PRs with unsigned commits cannot be
merged)
- [x] Tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] A _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (for bug
fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)
- [x] I have reviewed this pull request (self-review)

## Future Work

- Backport MAI-Voice-2.1 / 2.1-Flash to `release-v6.0`. The v6 provider
spec has no streaming transcription, so the backport is voice-only.

## Related Issues

Follows #21851 (MAI-Voice-2) and #21850 (MAI-Transcribe-1.5).

fix: accept structurally identical cross-realm tool approval inputs (#21810)

## Background

Manual tool approvals with unchanged, schema-valid JSON from another
JavaScript realm were rejected, preventing approved tools from executing
in workflow environments.

## Root Cause

isDeepEqualData compared constructor identity before JSON fields; Zod
produced a current-realm object whose constructor differed from the
cross-realm approved input, despite identical data.

## Summary

Updated deep JSON comparison to treat Object prototypes and arrays from
different realms as equivalent while retaining prototype checks for
non-JSON objects. Added an ai package patch changeset.

## Testing

Added a Node regression test covering tool approval validation for
cross-realm objects with nested arrays.

## End-to-end Validation

- `pnpm -C examples/ai-functions exec tsx
src/reproduction/issue-21805-cross-realm-tool-approval.ts` completed
successfully through immutable replay; the approval remained valid and
the tool executed.

## Related Issues

Fixes #21805

Closes #21806

feat(amazon-bedrock): add requestMetadata support for Converse and ConverseStream (#20415)

## Background

Bedrock supports a requestMetadata property that is stored in invocation
logs. It can be used with cloudwatch to query for cost attribution.

The current provider options/body don't allow passing it (that I can
see).

## Summary

Adds `requestMetadata` to `providerOptions.amazonBedrock` for the
Converse and ConverseStream APIs. The field maps directly to the
[Bedrock `requestMetadata` request body
parameter](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-request-metadata.html)
and is recorded in invocation logs for cost attribution.

## Usage

```ts
await generateText({
  model: bedrock('us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-20250514-v1:0'),
  providerOptions: {
    amazonBedrock: {
      requestMetadata: { team: 'search', environment: 'prod' },
    },
  },
  prompt: '...',
});
```

Changes
- `amazon-bedrock-chat-language-model-options.ts` — adds
`requestMetadata: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).optional()` to the
provider options schema
- `amazon-bedrock-api-types.ts` — adds `requestMetadata?: Record<string,
string> to AmazonBedrockConverseInput`
- `amazon-bedrock-chat-language-model.ts` — injects the value as a
top-level Converse body field; strips it from the
`filteredAmazonBedrockOptions` spread to prevent double-sending

## End-to-End Verification

I'm running this as a patch and can see the expected values in Bedrock
invocation logs.
